subject: Mythology
title: Witchcraft Beliefs in Africa
description: One-minute skill: Witchcraft Beliefs in Africa.

hook.text: In many African cultures, unexplained illness or misfortune is attributed to witchcraft by someone in your community.

buildup.text: Witchcraft is not magic spells. It is believed to be an invisible force inside certain people that causes harm.

discovery.text: The Azande of Central Africa built a full logical system for detecting witchcraft, documented by Evans-Pritchard.

twist.text: Witchcraft beliefs serve a social role: they explain suffering and enforce community norms through fear of accusation.

climax.text: These beliefs remain powerful today. Witch accusations still cause real harm in parts of Africa.

punchline.text: Witchcraft beliefs answer what science cannot: why did this happen to me?

quiz.question: What social function do witchcraft beliefs serve in African communities?
options: They explain suffering and enforce community norms through fear of accusation
They are purely religious with no social impact
